content:
In July of this year, Apple rolled out a basic search feature update for its TestFlight app. You might think such a simple update would be widely appreciated, but the same version of TestFlight also introduced a rather annoying bug for many users.

Personally, this bug didn’t affect me much. So I’m treating this TestFlight update as a small step, but a significant one.

Sometimes, a small change can have a big impact. This is especially true for users who have installed a large number of beta test apps — Apple’s latest TestFlight update is a clear example. Apple has just updated TestFlight across multiple platforms including iPhone, iPad, and Mac. The new version 4.3 adds a “search bar for quickly finding apps.”

Looking back, I did notice something unusual at the time and noted it at the end of the article (although my judgment then was the exact opposite of what it is now):

The reason I didn’t see it as a bug is that last year I merged two Apple accounts that used iCloud and the App Store separately, keeping my TestFlight app history accumulated over the years. The process wasn’t convenient, but I thought it was worth it.

In any case, the TestFlight bug wasn’t overlooked — John Vorhees of MacStories spotted it:

So when I saw Zac Hall’s article on 9to5Mac mentioning that TestFlight had finally added a search bar, you can imagine how excited I was. I thought, “Finally!” and immediately dropped what I was doing to update the app. […] But there’s a big “however” here. Previously, TestFlight betas were sorted in reverse chronological order, which is exactly the way I liked it. […] Now, expired betas and still-valid betas are all mixed together in alphabetical order, and the list of expired betas seems to have expanded to include every beta I’ve ever participated in. I did a rough count — for me, nearly 800 app entries. As you’d expect, very few of those betas are actually useful. The search feature does help, but you can no longer scroll through them one by one.

Later in August, John Gruber wrote an article on Daring Fireball discussing the TestFlight update and the bug:

Last night, more than a month after this bug appeared (and was raised by Vorhees), Apple finally updated TestFlight for the first time. Although the update notes only mention bug fixes, the update does indeed address the related bug.

TestFlight version 4.3.1 is exactly the fix provided for users affected by this regression.

Make the most of your Apple products
